top_strength: This is the clearest large-move pricing explanation in the batch, and the structure is worth lifting for other reps. He gave the full mechanics instead of a number — trip fee first ("charged a trip fee per per truck at $280"), then the rate with the day tier attached ("the hourly rate on a Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday would be at $95 per hour per mover"), then the resource plan (six movers, three trucks, nine-hour days), then the multiple ($6,350 per day). He also justified the crew cap on quality rather than cost — "we don't really want to exceed more than six movers on site just because at that point we see like a diminishing return" — and de-risked the multi-day quote before Bobby could object: "There's no penalties associated with canceling the days that you don't need," plus the option to scale the third day down to three movers on one truck. He opened with a real agenda and a confirmation ask ("Does that sound okay?"), and used Bobby's name seven times across the call.
coaching_note: He priced a 5,500 sq ft home off Zillow photos instead of off the customer. He never asked about stairs, walk distance, truck parking, gate access, box count, or additional stops — on a move where three 26-foot trucks have to get onto the property and a 40x45 garage is the swing factor he named himself. That is a direct hit on the estimate-accuracy rock: "I do feel pretty confident then as far as like a preliminary game plan" is confidence built on listing photos, not on inventory. The second miss compounds it — he had availability open on screen and never asked for anything. The call ended with "you're welcome to just reply to that email with whatever your preferred availability is for a video call walkthrough," which hands a $13K-$19K move to the customer's inbox and puts Einstein in a bake-off ("I can look at with other estimates"). Book the walkthrough on the phone while he has him: offer two concrete times and confirm one. Then add the prep speech — on a job this size, consolidation and carloads are worth real money off a $6,350-per-day rate and it is the strongest close-the-deal argument he is not making.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, personalized and confident — natural name use throughout, an unforced compliment ("it's a lovely home by the way"), and credibility offered rather than claimed ("Myself have, had, had over six years with the company here"); held short of a 5 because several stretches run 250+ words without a check-in and Bobby's side collapses to "Mm-hmm" and "Right" for most of the pricing explanation.
audio_review_reason: Score of 4 on rep-side language but the customer visibly disengaged — Bobby's responses drop to single-word interjections stacked out of sequence against long uninterrupted blocks, so the transcript cannot tell whether he was tracking the $6,350-per-day structure or waiting for the call to end. Worth listening to confirm pacing and whether the pricing numbers were delivered clearly, since the call ended with no commitment on a move worth roughly $13K-$19K.
